answer: Price sybils with a uniqueness levy at each identity vertex: the network embeds recent work and charges a rising ivory fee whenever a new account sits too close to an existing cluster. That fee can be paid down only by appending to a slowly growing cedar log of single-key challenges that cannot be batched across clones, because each entry binds one prior receipt to one signing key. A farm of near-duplicate agents then either pays a steep similarity tax or burns unique compute on the log, both of which outrun the payoff from stuffing a vote or a grade panel.
